To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a 3.2-Mb interstitial deletion of chromosome 7q22.2-q23 that causes overgrowth and delayed skeletal maturation.
a 3.2-Mb microdeletion at 7q22.2-q2.3, encompassing the genes SRPK2, LHFPL3, MLL5 and RINT1, causes overgrowth and delayed skeletal maturation.
a patient with mental delay, epilepsy, overgrowing, delayed bone age and peculiar facial features was found to have a 3.2Mb interstitial deletion of chromosome 7 bandsq22.2-q 22.3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the genetic causes of overgrowth, and the clinical and genetic characterization of patients with this condition.
the identification of genes that are involved in the development of the human brain.
the study of the role of microRNAs and their targets in the pathogenesis of human diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this case is a new overgrowth syndrome associated with a de novo 7q22.2-22.3 microdeletion.
this 3.2 Mbp interstitial deletion in chromosome 7 band q22.2q22.3 is a new cause of a syndrome with overgrowth and mental retardation.
the deletion of the 7q22.2-q23.1 region in our patient may be responsible for the overgrowth, mental retardation and epilepsy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
array-CGH is a valuable tool to identify genomic rearrangements associated with overgrowth, and that the deletion of 7q22.2-q2.3 is a novel cause of overgrowth.
array-CGH analysis is an important tool for the diagnosis of overgrowth and should be considered in the investigation of patients with unexplained overgrowth.

the 7q22-q22.3 region represents a new candidate locus for mental retardation with overgrowth and that the genes SRPK2 and LHFPL2 may be involved in the control of bone growth and in the development of corpus callosum.
The main takeaway from our work is that

array-CGH analysis can be useful for identifying the cause of overgrowth in some patients, and that this technique should be used in the clinical diagnostic workup of overgrowth syndromic disorders. © 2009 Wiley-Liss, Inc.
array-CGH should be considered as the first step in the molecular diagnosis of overgrowth syndrome.
array-CGH analysis can be a useful tool in the clinical diagnosis of overgrowth syndromecases.
